label: v130
changes: A Display size slider in Hub settings. It scales everything — text, icons, buttons, spacing — not just the words, in five steps. Per device, so your phone and your laptop can disagree.

The header is one line now instead of three. The hub name IS the menu: tap it for spaces, settings, backup and sign out. It used to be a title, a pill repeating that same title underneath it, and a permanent row of six unlabelled icons.
Sections are just the burger button — the icon, the current section name and the arrow beside it were four ways of saying one thing.
Add a person now sits beside the list of people rather than up in the app header.
Fixed: when sign-in failed, nothing happened at all — the reason only ever went to the developer console. It now tells you what went wrong and what to do about it.
Fixed: after an update, the app could show the sign-in screen for a long time even though you were already signed in. It was waiting on a slow first read before it would admit it knew who you were.
The grey line at the top of a pop-up is now a real handle — grab it and swipe down to close. It has looked draggable since the day it was drawn; now it is, in all 23 places it appears.

You can collapse the family list. With eight people you were scrolling past the whole household to reach one person. Tap the member count to fold it down to whoever you're looking at, and it stays folded until you unfold it.
Fixed: the page background is now painted on the document itself. On desktop, a window resize could leave a strip of app beside a band of plain white.
The app is now called Teluva. Same app, same data, nothing to do at your end — you'll see the new name and icon. If you've added it to your Home Screen, the icon will refresh on its own
A guided setup the first time you sign in: it asks the fifteen or so things worth knowing, in the order a person would actually ask them. Stop halfway and it picks up where you left off

It now offers to add itself to your Home Screen — which is also the only way an iPhone will let it send you a birthday or expiry reminder. It asks once, backs off if you say no, and stops asking after the third time
